---
title: "Evaluate a random Gridworld policy"
toc: false
page-layout: full
---

The Gridworld now has a fixed policy: from every state, the agent chooses up,
right, down, or left with probability (0.25). With the policy fixed, the
environment is a Markov reward process. The state value $V_k(s)$ estimates
the expected discounted return from state $s$ after $k$ synchronous Bellman
backups.

For this random policy and $\gamma=0.9$, one backup is

$$
V_{k+1}(s)=\frac{1}{4}\sum_a\left[r(s,a,s')+0.9V_k(s')\right].
$$

::: {.callout-tip}
## What to watch

Begin with $V_0(s)=0$. A Bellman sweep updates every state from the *previous*
value grid. Watch the positive values from A and B, and the boundary penalty,
spread through the grid over repeated sweeps.
:::
